mlag.note: Two independent Nexus switches form a vPC domain for active/active multichassis link aggregation, over a peer link built from front-panel Ethernet ports. Each peer keeps its own control and management plane; this is not a stack

stacking.note: No hardware stacking. Nexus switches are deployed as independent systems; multichassis redundancy is vPC

routing.summary: NX-OS Layer 3: static, OSPFv2/v3, IS-IS, EIGRP, RIPv2, BGP/MP-BGP, PIM-SM/SSM, MSDP, HSRP, VRRP, VXLAN BGP EVPN, Segment Routing. Layer 3 unicast and multicast routing require a license beyond the default Layer 2 feature set

licensing: Default system software covers Layer 2 security and management. Layer 3 unicast and multicast routing and Nexus Data Broker need additional licensing; sold as Data Center Networking (DCN) Essentials, Advantage or Premier subscriptions, or perpetual. These switches ship licensed for any 24 of the 48 downlink ports; a 48-port upgrade license (N9K-FX3-24P-UPG=, N9K-FX-24P-UPG= or N9K-EX-24P-UPG=) unlocks the rest. MACsec on the FX-24 models needs a feature license
routeScale: FX3H and FX-24: 1,792,000 LPM routes and IP host entries. EX-24: 896,000
macsec: Wire-rate MACsec on all ports of the FX-24 models (feature license required); not stated for the FX3H or EX-24 models

power.summary: Up to two hot-swappable power supplies and four hot-swappable fans, port-side intake or exhaust. FX3H: 650W AC, 930W DC or 1200W HVAC/HVDC. 93108TC-FX3H: 1100W or 1900W AC. FX-24 and EX-24: 500W AC, 930W DC or 1200W HVAC/HVDC

note: Compact-licensing variants of the 9300-EX, FX and FX3 leaf switches for smaller deployments. Each has 48 physical downlink ports but ships licensed to use any 24 of them, so accessPorts here record the 24 licensed ports, not the physical 48
verifyNote: accessPorts record the 24 licensed downlinks; the hardware has 48 physical ports and a 48-port upgrade license is orderable. Cisco does not publish switching capacity or forwarding rate for the 24-port models on this data sheet
